summary: Nyoten Jimbo (1880–1946) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Baisen Azegami. He held a professorship at Komazawa University.

Ole Holten Pind (1945–2018) worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He earned his Dr.phil. at the University of Vienna under Ernst Steinkellner (~2003–2009) and later served as a professor at the University of Hamburg.

Oleg Grabar (1929–2011) was a historian and archaeologist. He studied at the University of Paris (~1946–1948), Harvard (~1948–1950), and Princeton (~1950–1955), later holding posts at the University of Michigan (~1954–1969) and Harvard (~1969–1990).

Oliver Codrington (1837–1921) was an archaeologist, historian, and Indologist. He served as Secretary of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (attested 1878) and Honorary Librarian of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland (attested 1892).

Oliver Hector de Alwis Wijesekera (1909–1990) specialized in Indology and Buddhist studies, studying at the University of Ceylon and SOAS under William Stede. He served at the University of Ceylon, Smith College, Harvard, and the University of Pennsylvania.
Oliver Philipp Frey works in the fields of Indology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Vienna and later held an academic post there.

Olivier Lacombe (1904–2001) worked in philosophy, Indology, and religious studies. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure (~1925–1928) and the Faculty of Arts of Paris (~1930–1939), later teaching at Paris (~1959–1970) and Paris-Sorbonne University (~1970–1974).

Olle Qvarnström (b. 1953) is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy who studied at Copenhagen, Harvard, and Washington, and under Tord Olsson. He held a post at Lund University (attested 2000–2005).

Om Prakash is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who completed a PhD at the University of Delhi under Dasharatha Sharma. He held posts at Kirori Mal College (attested 1961) and the University of Delhi (attested 2003).

Orna Almogi specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Ngagyur Nyingma Institute under Khenpo Wangchuk Sonam and under David P. Jackson and Lambert Schmithausen, later working at the Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project and University of Hamburg.

Osamu Hayashima (b. 1946) specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied under Noritoshi Aramaki and at the University of Hamburg (1992), later holding professorships at Nagasaki University, Shiga University of Medical Science, and Ryukoku University.

Osamu Takata (1907–1991) worked in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. He studied under Baiei Henmi and later served as head of the fine arts department at the Tokyo National Research Institute for Cultural Properties.
Oscar Botto (1922–2008) was an Indologist who studied at the University of Turin from around 1941 to 1945. He also founded the journal Indologica Taurinensia.

Oskar von Hinüber (b. 1939) is an Indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and linguist. He studied at Mainz, directed the Nepal Research Centre, and held professorships at the University of Mainz (~1973–1981) and the University of Freiburg (~1981–2006).

Osmund Bopearachchi (b. 1949) is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied under Paul Bernard (~1983–1987) and held a post at the Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique (attested 2015).

Osvald Sirén (1879–1966) was a scholar of Sinology and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Helsinki (~1897–1900) and held posts at Stockholm University (1908–1923) and the Nationalmuseum (1928–1945).

Othmar Frank (1770–1840) was an Indologist, philosopher, and Iranian studies scholar who studied in Paris and London. He held professorships at the University of Bamberg (~1803–1808), University of Würzburg (~1821–1826), and Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (1826).
Otoya Tanaka (1903–1989) was an Indologist who studied under Naoshiro Tsuji at the University of Tokyo (~1924–1927). He later held a post at Chuo University (~1964–1974).
Otto Blau (1828–1879) worked in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Halle-Wittenberg under August Friedrich Pott between ~1848 and 1852.
Otto Fischer (1886–1948) specialized in Sinology, Japanology, and history/archaeology. He held posts at the Kunstmuseum Basel in 1927 and at the University of Basel from ~1927 to 1937.
